title: Engelbrektsloppet Race Prep - Lower Body & Core Strength

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly through spinal flexion and extension. Sync movement with breathing—inhale on cow, exhale on cat. Focus on mobilizing the entire spine.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Sit with both legs at 90 degrees. Switch leg positions smoothly, keeping hips grounded. This preps hip mobility for the 45km race demands.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.cues: Extend opposite arm and leg while maintaining a neutral spine. Move with control—no momentum. Activates core and glutes essential for trail running.

items.name: Back Squat
items.cues: Heavy compound movement for lower body power. Drive through heels, keep chest up, depth at or below parallel. Rest fully between sets for CNS recovery.

items.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
items.cues: Rear foot elevated, front knee tracks over ankle. Drives unilateral leg strength critical for trail stability. Controlled descent, powerful drive up.

items.name: Cable Core Press
items.cues: Standing, press away from body against cable resistance. Resist rotation. Builds anti-rotational core strength for uneven terrain engagement.

items.name: Bent Over Row
items.cues: Hip hinge position, chest high. Row weight to lower ribs, squeeze shoulder blades. Upper back strength supports posture during long race efforts.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Keep heel grounded, lean forward into the wall. Hold stretch to mild tension—30 seconds per side. Critical for trail running ankle stability.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Arm elevated against wall, shoulder externally rotated. Releases shoulder tension from rowing work. Hold for 30 seconds per side.

items.name: Adductor Rockbacks
items.cues: Wide-legged position, rock hips back to stretch inner thighs. Gentle dynamic stretch to recover from intense lower body work.

rationale: With 20 days until Engelbrektsloppet 45km, this strength session targets lower body power and unilateral stability critical for trail terrain. Back squats and Bulgarian split squats build the glute and quad strength needed for sustained climbing and descent control.

Recent training shows emphasis on mobility and endurance; this workout complements that with heavy compound lifts at RPE 6-7 intensity, maintaining neuromuscular adaptation while staying within recovery constraints.

Core pressing and rowing work strengthen anti-rotational stability and posture endurance—essential for maintaining form over 45km on variable terrain. The 25-minute window with full recovery periods ensures quality over volume as the race approaches.
